subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Inside a Crash Test
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Inside a Crash Test.

hook.text: A crash test dummy costs over $500,000 and contains hundreds of sensors across its body.

buildup.text: Engineers strap the dummy into a car, then launch it into a concrete wall at a set speed.

discovery.text: Sensors in the head, chest, and legs measure exact forces to predict real human injuries.

twist.text: Until 2022, most crash test dummies were modeled only on the body of an average-sized man.

climax.text: New female and child-sized dummies are finally being used to make cars safer for everyone.

punchline.text: For decades, crash safety was designed for one body type.

quiz.question: What was a key limitation of crash test dummies until recently?

details.summary: Modern crash tests slam vehicles into barriers, poles, and simulated oncoming cars at precise speeds while instrumented dummies record the forces transmitted to a human body during impact.
details.whyItMatters: Crash testing has transformed car safety from guesswork to engineering science, giving manufacturers data-driven feedback that has steadily reduced occupant injury severity over decades.
takeaways: Dummies carry dozens of sensors measuring force and acceleration
Tests include frontal, side, rear, and pole impact scenarios
Results directly influence vehicle design before production

faq.question: How much does a crash test dummy cost?
faq.answer: A modern crash test dummy like the THOR model can cost over half a million dollars due to the dozens of precision sensors embedded throughout its body to measure forces during impact.

faq.question: Are real cars destroyed in every crash test?
faq.answer: Yes. Each physical crash test destroys the vehicle, which is why manufacturers also rely heavily on computer simulations to test thousands of scenarios virtually before building prototype cars.
